name: commons-take-1
description: ⭐ THE OUTFLOW CAP, AND THE ONLY SEMANTIC THAT CAN WORK, AT 1 (Dean, 09/09/2026). rules.economy.commonsHarvestTake 1: a central harvest takes at most the most recently played 1 card - the TOP of the pile - and LEAVES THE REST STANDING in the centre. A pile shallower than that gives up all of it, so the rule is “at most 1” and never a minimum. The shipped rule is null: the whole pile comes (C5). Dean, 09/09/2026: “Can we measure how many cards are taken when the Harvest is done against the centre cards? I'm interested to see if we place a threshold on the centre cards if it will reduce the number of cards going from the centre to the barns - my target is about 30-40% of barn cards should come from the middle.” The centre share reads 63.1% on the shipped rules. ⛔ THE FIRST ANSWER MEASURED NOTHING, WHICH IS WHY THERE ARE THREE SEMANTICS AND NOT ONE. rules.economy.commonsThreshold at 2 - a cap on the INFLOW - moved the centre share by 0.1 points, 63.1% to 63.0%, for two reasons worth holding on to before running any of these: a central harvest already takes a MEDIAN OF TWO CARDS, so a cap of two caps almost nothing; and the centre is a CLOSED system, in by a play (C3) and out by a harvest (D3), so every card played into it reaches somebody's barn unless the game ends first. A cap on plays therefore changes WHEN cards leave the centre, not how many. ⭐ THE THREE SEMANTICS, NAMED SO NOBODY CONFUSES THEM: commonsThreshold caps the INFLOW (a pile at its cap refuses a play); commonsHarvestMin gates the OUTFLOW (a pile below n refuses a harvest - the BUILDING semantic, a pile is “full” at n); commonsHarvestTake caps the SIZE of the outflow and leaves the rest standing, which is the only one of the three that can reduce the centre's outflow WITHOUT reducing plays. ⚠️ READ EVERY ONE OF THEM AGAINST THE CONSERVATION LINE a18 PRINTS, which carries all three terms per game: plays into the centre = cards harvested out + cards stranded at game end. A knob that hits Dean's target by STRANDING cards has changed where the cards end up rather than how the centre feeds a barn during play, and that is a different answer to his question. ⚠️ AND SWEEP THEM ONE AT A TIME. Each of these files sets exactly ONE leaf and carries no passengers, which is the 05/09/2026 lesson: a joint move is unattributable. ⭐ WHY THIS ONE IS DIFFERENT FROM THE OTHER TWO, IN ONE SENTENCE: the cards it does not take stay in the centre, so it is the only rule of the three that reduces the outflow without reducing the plays that feed it. At 1 the centre stops being a fat prize altogether and becomes a one-card-a-turn faucet for everybody, which is a different game and not only a different number: a pile can never be worth racing for, and the Harvest action loses the one target that was not on your own farm. ⚠️ ITS OWN FAILURE MODE IS THE STRANDED COLUMN. If the share falls because cards pile up in the middle and never leave, the game has grown a card SINK rather than a smaller faucet, and 105 cards is the whole supply - watch reshuffles and the deck-dry end reason beside a18. READ IN THIS ORDER: (1) a18's centre share of harvested barn cards, pooled and by seat count, against the 30-40% target; (2) the conservation line, to see whether the share moved by harvesting less or by stranding more; (3) the distribution of cards taken per central harvest (1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5+), which says what any cap had to work with; (4) a17's bonus rate against Dean's 30-60% band, because a knob that makes the centre less rewarding can push plays out of the band at the other end; (5) the barn glut (a06) and deliveries per player, since the centre is a barn faucet and every one of these is a tap on it.
